alex: Hey team — I'm sketching a migration path for Dedicated customers to move from pure static reserved pools -> hybrid reserved+ephemeral credits. Goal: reduce committed GPU footprint while protecting SLA for long-tail enterprise workloads. I want feedback on runway, operator controls, and billing UX. TL;DR below, short Qs after. :wave:

alex: TL;DR plan: 1) Baseline reserved capacity = 60-80% of current commit. 2) Ephemeral credits bucket for spikes (billing: pay-as-you-go credits charged monthly). 3) Safety net: automatic short-term top-up if latency SLO degradation > threshold for 3m. 4) 6-month opt-in phase with grandfathered pricing and telemetry gating.

maria: curious about the safety-net trigger — how aggressive is the auto top-up? we need clear thresholds to avoid oscillation. also worried about cache warming costs when switching to ephemeral nodes. :thinking_face:

samir: agree on oscillation risk. suggest: safety-net requires (a) sustained P95 increase > 30% AND (b) queue depth > X for 90s. top-up should be single short burst (eg +1-2 nodes) with cooldown 15m. also plan preemption credits so reserved tasks aren't evicted.

alex: good, that matches what I was thinking. propose thresholds in config as defaults but editable per-customer:  p95_multiplier=1.3, sustained_window=180s, cooldown=900s.

alex: sample config snippet we'll expose in console:
```
hybrid_reserve:
  base_commit_pct: 0.7
  ephemeral_bucket_tokens: 10000  # token = 1-second-of-GPU at baseline perf
  safety_net:
    p95_mult: 1.3
    window_s: 180
    cooldown_s: 900
```

maria: thanks — can we add a KV/pre-warm hint to ephemeral boots so we reduce tail latency? maybe injection of cached prefixes for top customers.

samir: technically doable: snapshot a tiny KV preload for the top N models per tenant. risk: extra memory + longer boot time. we'd gate preload to customers with >Y QPS or on canary.

tj: from sales — customers will ask two things: (1) what happens to their committed units for billing/discounts, (2) will they be bumped during peak? Need clear language: grandfathered discounts for 6 months + a dashboard showing ephemeral spend and projected monthly bill. Also add an opt-out flow. :raised_hand:

kelly: finance input — we need a modeling doc before we announce. two scenarios: conservative (most keep >80% commit) vs optimistic (most drop to 50%). attach sample numbers later, but early ask: get monthly cohort-level projections and worst-case uplift for credits.

alex: noted. I'll draft a pricing model spreadsheet. For rollout gating: telemetry we need = per-tenant p95 trend, ephemeral spend, safety-net triggers, post-top-up latency delta. keep canary to 5 tenants first.

maria: can we also add a fast rollback if top-up doesn't help within 2m? e.g., fallback to model variant (smaller) or route to hosted fallback to preserve SLO.

samir: yes — fallback policies should be first-class: route_to_fallback_model, or migrate to a compatible lower-cost GPU pool. we'll add an operator override to force-failback.

ops-bot: new saga created: /sagas HYBRID-ONRAMP-1776543210 — owners: alex, maria, samir. Actions: PRD draft, infra prototype, pricing model, canary list.

alex: proposed next steps: (1) I'll write PRD by EOD Fri, (2) infra prototyping next sprint (samir + maria), (3) finance model (kelly), (4) sales messaging draft (tj). please reply with owners or objections. :rocket:
